title: European registry investigating the association between energy delivered by mechanical ventilation and major clinical outcomes in preterm infants
official: Mechanical power and major clinical outcomes in extremely preterm neonates
summary:
Background and study aims
Mechanical power (MP) is the energy delivered by a mechanical ventilator to the lungs of critically ill patients over a given amount of time.  MP is calculated using equations that incorporate the parameters employed to configure ventilators during clinical care. A large body of evidence shows that MP and its components are linked to negative outcomes (such as mortality) in critically ill adults. This is because excessive energy can damage the lungs, so it is important to keep ventilation 'gentle' while ensuring sufficient respiratory support. There are only limited data available for neonates. Previously, we demonstrated that MP is easy to calculate at the bedside and that it may be associated with death or bronchopulmonary dysplasia, a chronic respiratory disorder affecting infants born prematurely. This study therefore aims to verify the existence of this association.

Who can participate?
Extremely preterm infants who are intubated and ventilated using the most common ventilatory modes

What does the study involve?
Only the collection of routinely available ventilatory parameters and clinical date

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
There is absolutely no risk to participants. The benefits will be for the wider society and for babies who are born prematurely in future, as we will be better able to provide them with tailored ventilation.

Where is the study run from?
From several referral neonatal intensive care units in Europe

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
Starting in December 2026 and running at least 1-1.5 year depending on the birth and recruitment rate 

Who is funding the study?
There is no funding  dedicated to the study. The study is conducted within the working hours of investigators 

Who is the main contact?
Dr. Almudena Alonso - Ojembarrena, Hospital Puerta del Mar (Cadiz - Spain)
Prof. Daniele De Luca, APHP-Paris Saclay University Hospital (Paris, France) 
and all the local investigators in each contributing center

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Gestational age <=28 weeks 
2. Invasive conventional mechanical ventilation at any time during the NICU hospitalisation and before 36 weeks post- menstrual age
Exclusion criteria:
1. Ventilated with non-conventional modes (e.g. HFOV, HFPV, HFJV)
2. Major congenital malformations
3. Chromosomal abnormalities
4. Congenital lung disorders
5. Perinatal asphyxia leading to death within the first 72h of life
